text:
sam: Heads-up — new customer account (acme-biz) onboarding. They need dedicated GPU capacity in us-west-2 behind a private VPC. Asking for infra setup and quota increases so we don't get blocked during provisioning.

matt: OK — what does acme need exactly? GPU types / counts, and networking constraints?

sam: Initial ask: 6 x p4d instances (we'll scale later), private subnets per AZ, no public IPs on GPUs, egress via central NAT/TGW. Also need interface endpoints for S3 and ECR via PrivateLink equivalents.

jess: Sounds good. Two immediate quota items we need to request from AWS: EC2 On-Demand for p4d in us-west-2 (target 6) and EIP limit bump (we use EIPs for NAT HA). Also ENI/secondary IP quotas because p4d uses many ENIs.

oliver: For IP planning, propose hub VPC 10.200.0.0/20 (shared services + NAT), and a tenant VPC 10.201.0.0/22 for acme compute. Split compute by AZ with /24s for GPU subnets so we can isolate and control AZ affinity. That gives us room for future tenants.

matt: FYI NAT gateways are expensive at scale. If acme streams a lot of data we should consider central egress with NAT + prefix lists and avoid per-spoke NAT. Also look at NAT Gateway hourly + data processing cost.

jess: Agreed. We'll place NATs in the hub VPC (one per AZ) and attach spokes via TGW. TGW route propagation to the hub route table, and static routes from hub to spokes. Need TGW attachments quota increase? We might need new VPN/Attachment counts.

sam: Can someone open the support cases? Steps I want: 1) Request EC2 On-Demand quota for p4d to 6 in us-west-2; 2) Increase Elastic IPs from 50 -> 200 in us-west-2; 3) Increase ENI per region/instance soft limit to support p4d networking; 4) TGW attachments limit bump if needed; 5) Service Quotas for VPC route table entries if we anticipate many prefixes.

matt: I'll open the support cases. Quick note: for ENIs the quota we care about is "Elastic network interfaces (ENI) per region" and "IPv4 addresses per ENI". p4d24xlarge uses multiple ENIs for placement groups; check instance type docs.

infra-bot: Reminder: include creation justification and expected steady-state usage in AWS support case text to speed approvals. Example: "Production inference cluster for enterprise customer, initial fleet 6 p4d, scaling to 24 over 6 months; private networking via TGW; business-critical SLAs."

jess: Also need to update our terraform modules: spoke VPC module must support attach_to_tgw flag, and subnet sizing variables (/24 for gpu_subnet_size). I'll open a PR after CIDR lock.

oliver: Quick routing note — use route-table per AZ for GPU subnets so we can direct-specific AZ NAT failover and avoid cross-AZ SNAT churn. Also ensure source/dest checks disabled on NAT instances if we go that route.

matt: Opened support cases: 1887654321-aws-case-ec2-quota, 1887654322-aws-case-eips, 1887654323-aws-case-eni. I've pasted request IDs in the cases. Keeping the customer justification as infra-bot suggested.

sam: Thanks. Can someone confirm expected lead time? We should schedule provisioning tasks after quotas are approved.

sre-oncall: Typical quota approvals are 24–72h for soft limits; specialized GPU fleet increases (p4d) can take longer — include billing/account manager CC to expedite. Also double-check dedicated capacity offers (Savings or Dedicated Host) if they need long-term reserved instances — that impacts procurement.

jess: I'll lock CIDRs and open the TF PR today. Assigning tasks: matt -> follow up on support cases and escalate if no reply in 48h; jess -> terraform + subnet plan; oliver -> network diagrams and TGW route tables. sam -> coordinate with sales/ops for account billing info for the support cases.

matt: Noted. I'll post case numbers & any AWS replies here. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks all. If anyone spots a gotcha (security or cost), flag it here early.

infra-bot: Action items created: #1234 (matt) support case follow-ups, #1235 (jess) terraform PR, #1236 (oliver) network diagram.
